title: Pitch Angle Library
description: Curated library of pitch angles (hooks) the AI generation pipeline draws from when composing per-contact outreach emails. Each angle has trigger conditions (when it applies), role/step applicability, a strength score, and example phrasing the LLM adapts. Live data lives at `data/pitch_angles.json`. See `docs/outreach_workflow.md` for how angles plug into the generation step.

agency_id.description: Multi-tenant scope: FK to agency_profile.agency_id. Optional in v0.1 (single-tenant deploys may omit); required in v2 SaaS. When present, all cross-record queries MUST filter by agency_id to prevent cross-tenant data leakage. See docs/data_lineage.md GAP-01/02 for rationale.

angles.description: All authored angles. Order doesn't matter — orchestrator filters and sorts by strength_score at runtime.

angle_id.description: Stable snake_case identifier. Used in `pitch_enrollment.steps[].generation_meta.angles_used` for A/B analytics.

description.description: One-paragraph explanation of when and why this angle works.

type.description: Type of trigger condition. The orchestrator has a Python function per type that returns {fires: bool, merge_field_values: {...}} given the (talent, contact, brand) context. New trigger types require both a code update and an enum extension.

config.description: Trigger-specific configuration. Free-form by design; each trigger type's evaluator interprets it.

applicable_to_decision_roles.description: Which `decision_role` values this angle can be used for. The 5-value taxonomy matches `schemas/brand_contact.schema.json`.

applicable_to_steps.description: Which step numbers in a sequence this angle suits. Step 1 = first touch (strongest angles); later steps reserved for different angles to avoid repetition.

authored_strength_score.description: Hand-authored expected effectiveness. Used by the orchestrator when ranking candidate angles for an email. Updated manually as the user learns what works (v0.1); auto-tuned from observed reply data in v2.

example_phrasing.description: Template sentence pattern the LLM adapts. Merge fields in `{curly_braces}`. The LLM rewrites for tone/context, not copy-pastes.

merge_fields_required.description: Dot-path data fields the trigger evaluator must return for this angle to be usable (e.g. `competitor_brand`, `campaign_metric`). If any required field is null after evaluation, the angle is skipped.

pair_well_with.description: Other `angle_id`s that work well as a supporting angle when this is the primary. The LLM may use one supporting angle alongside the primary.

avoid_combining_with.description: Other `angle_id`s that would feel redundant or clash. The orchestrator never picks both.

notes.description: Free-text guidance for human review (rationale, edge cases, tone guidance).
